findings.claim: The change deletes `this.HashCollisionResistant = copyFrom.HashCollisionResistant;` from the MessagePackSecurity copy constructor. This has nothing to do with REQ-2297. Every clone (for example `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(n)`, or any derived security object) now silently drops collision-resistant hashing. Untrusted-data deserialization becomes exposed to hash-collision DoS again, which reverses the secure-by-default work recorded in L4.

receipt_plan.detail: In a MessagePack.Tests unit test, assert `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(10).HashCollisionResistant == true`. Also assert that `GetEqualityComparer<string>()` on the clone does not return the default comparer. Expected: passes on base, fails on head.

findings.claim: The requirement says ALL generated code is decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. It only allows conditional emission where the attribute does not exist. The change wraps every attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so it is never emitted for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework consumers. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+. Generated code for those major targets stays undecorated and keeps skewing coverage, so the requirement is unmet for them.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/ExcludeFromCodeCoverageOnDownlevelTargetsTests.cs (GeneratedTypesAreExcludedWhenTargetSymbolDefined). It runs the generator with parse-option symbols NETSTANDARD2_0 / NETFRAMEWORK defined and asserts that every generated type carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. Expected: fails on head. The same guard appears in EnumTemplate.tt:8, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt:18, UnionTemplate.tt:10, ResolverTemplate.tt:14/31/48 and CompositeResolverTemplate.tt:7/35.

findings.claim: The new README text says the attribute is not available on `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework. That is false: ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute ships in netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+. The docs justify the coverage gap described in the previous finding with an incorrect statement.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile `[System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] class C {}` in a project targeting netstandard2.0 and one targeting net472. Both compile, which contradicts README.md:1640.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Always emit `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on every generated formatter and resolver type. There is no setting and no opt-out; the templates write the attribute unconditionally, apart from the preprocessor guard.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Emit the attribute by default but add an opt-out setting. Add a bool option, for example `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` defaulting to true, to the generator's options model, read from an MSBuild/analyzer-config property or a resolver attribute property. Wrap each template's attribute line in `<# if (Options.Generator.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage) { #> ... <# } #>` and regenerate the .cs templates. Add snapshot tests for both the on and off states.
